newsitem.title: UK: European VGO weaker with crude's fall.
newsitem.headline: European VGO weaker with crude's fall.

text.p: Rising positive sentiment in the European vacuum gas oil market quickly dissipated on Wednesday after crude oil futures came off, traders said.
But despite the closing transatlantic arb, one low sulphur VGO cargo was reported sold out of Scandinavia into the United States but the seller said the deal was private and confidential.
Offers for low sulphur cargoes fob NWE were still in the $115 a tonne region but buyers were now below $110, shedding some $4-$5 from the end of last week's price, traders said.
"I guess the positive sentiment was there up until NYMEX opened, but now in terms of the fixed price numbers people are not going to be there anymore," one trader said.

"Unfortunately, when you move down 160 (1.6 cents a gallon) on Mogas that's like $4.50 on VGO in Northwest Europe. So unfortunately it was developing quiet well and people were keen on VGO discounts coming in the States but the arb again moved away," the trader added.
Demand from Europe was thin, they added.
Not too much activity was reported in high sulphur VGO cargoes, with traders putting the bid and ask levels at $5 below low sulphur.
